title: Requirements, SLOs & Capacity
description: Study translate requirements into measurable goals, latency budgets and percentiles, traffic estimates and concurrency, and quality-cost pareto trade-offs. Each lesson includes a worked example and an applied practice task.

lessons.title: Translate requirements into measurable goals
lessons.description: Write three functional requirements and three measurable service objectives.
lessons.conceptOverview: A design starts with user tasks, quality thresholds, traffic assumptions and operational constraints. Separate functional requirements from latency, availability and cost targets so trade-offs can be evaluated explicitly.
lessons.whyItMatters: Quality and operational requirements must both shape the architecture.
lessons.engineerDeepDive: A design starts with user tasks, quality thresholds, traffic assumptions and operational constraints. Separate functional requirements from latency, availability and cost targets so trade-offs can be evaluated explicitly.

lessons.title: Latency budgets and percentiles
lessons.description: Assign stage deadlines and define a trace-based end-to-end percentile measurement.
lessons.conceptOverview: Allocate an end-to-end deadline across retrieval, model work and downstream tools. Tail latency matters because averages hide slow requests; component percentiles cannot simply be added to obtain an exact end-to-end percentile.
lessons.whyItMatters: Measure end-to-end tails and bound stage deadlines.

lessons.title: Traffic estimates and concurrency
lessons.description: Estimate concurrency for a traffic burst and define an admission policy.
lessons.conceptOverview: Use arrival rate and service time to estimate in-flight work under stable conditions. Account for bursts, output length and admission limits; average throughput estimates are insufficient for overload planning.
lessons.whyItMatters: Capacity planning needs service time and burst assumptions.

lessons.title: Quality-cost Pareto trade-offs
lessons.description: Create a comparison table and identify dominated configurations.
lessons.conceptOverview: Compare configurations on a fixed workload using quality, latency and cost together. A configuration is dominated if another is no worse on every measured objective and better on at least one.
lessons.whyItMatters: Choose configurations using measured task-specific trade-offs.
